name: 1 Peter
description: Living hope · shared belonging · unequal power · gentle witness · willing care

1.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen ones who are living as foreigners in the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, that you may obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood: Grace to you and peace be multiplied.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes, even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently. They prophesied of the grace that would come to you,
searching for who or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them pointed to when he predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow them.

To them it was revealed that they served not themselves, but you, in these things, which now have been announced to you through those who preached the Good News to you by the Holy Spirit sent out from heaven; which things angels desire to look into.
Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
as children of obedience, not conforming yourselves according to your former lusts as in your ignorance,
but just as he who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior,
because it is written, “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
If you call on him as Father, who without respect of persons judges according to each man’s work, pass the time of your living as foreigners here in reverent fear,
knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things like silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers,
but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ,
who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in this last age for your sake,
who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.
Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently,
having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and remains forever.
For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls;
but the Lord’s word endures forever.” This is the word of Good News which was preached to you.

2.text: Putting away therefore all wickedness, all deceit, hypocrisies, envies, and all evil speaking,
as newborn babies, long for the pure spiritual milk, that with it you may grow,
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is gracious.
Come to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.
You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
Because it is contained in Scripture, “Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious. He who believes in him will not be disappointed.”
For you who believe therefore is the honor, but for those who are disobedient, “The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone,”
and, “a stumbling stone and a rock of offense.” For they stumble at the word, being disobedient, to which also they were appointed.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, that you may proclaim the excellence of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
In the past, you were not a people, but now are God’s people, who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
Beloved, I beg you as foreigners and pilgrims to abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul,
having good behavior among the nations, so in that of which they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good works and glorify God in the day of visitation.
Therefore subject yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake: whether to the king, as supreme,
or to governors, as sent by him for vengeance on evildoers and for praise to those who do well.
For this is the will of God, that by well-doing you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish men.
Live as free people, yet not using your freedom for a cloak of wickedness, but as bondservants of God.
Honor all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.
Servants, be in subjection to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the wicked.
For it is commendable if someone endures pain, suffering unjustly, because of conscience toward God.
For what glory is it if, when you sin, you patiently endure beating? But if when you do well, you patiently endure suffering, this is commendable with God.
For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps,
who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.”
When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
For you were going astray like sheep; but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

3.text: In the same way, wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, so that, even if any don’t obey the Word, they may be won by the behavior of their wives without a word,
seeing your pure behavior in fear.
Let your beauty come not from the outward adorning of braiding your hair, and of wearing gold ornaments or of putting on fine clothing,
but from the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptible adornment of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious in God’s sight.
For this is how in the past the holy women who hoped in God also adorned themselves, being in subjection to their own husbands.
So Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, whose children you now are if you do well and are not put in fear by any terror.

You husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, giving honor to the woman as to the weaker vessel, as also being joint heirs of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.
Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, courteous,
not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.
For, “He who would love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
Let him turn away from evil and do good. Let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears open to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
Now who will harm you if you become imitators of that which is good?
But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t fear what they fear, neither be troubled.”
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
having a good conscience. Thus, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disappointed who curse your good way of life in Christ.
For it is better, if it is God’s will, that you suffer for doing what is right than for doing evil.
Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit,
in whom he also went and preached to the spirits in prison,
who before were disobedient when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ship was being built. In it, few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.
This is a symbol of baptism, which now saves you—not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers being made subject to him.

4.text: Therefore, since Christ suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same mind; for he who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,
that you no longer should live the rest of your time in the flesh for the lusts of men, but for the will of God.
For we have spent enough of our past time doing the desire of the Gentiles, and having walked in lewdness, lusts, drunken binges, orgies, carousings, and abominable idolatries.
They think it is strange that you don’t run with them into the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you.
They will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For to this end the Good News was preached even to the dead, that they might be judged indeed as men in the flesh, but live as to God in the spirit.
But the end of all things is near. Therefore be of sound mind, self-controlled, and sober in prayer.
And above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, don’t be astonished at the fiery trial which has come upon you to test you, as though a strange thing happened to you.
But because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, that at the revelation of his glory you also may rejoice with exceeding joy.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you. On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.
But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evil doer, or a meddler in other men’s matters.
But if one of you suffers for being a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God in this matter.
For the time has come for judgment to begin with the household of God. If it begins first with us, what will happen to those who don’t obey the Good News of God?
“If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?”
Therefore let them also who suffer according to the will of God in doing good entrust their souls to him, as to a faithful Creator.

5.text: Therefore I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and who will also share in the glory that will be revealed:
shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly;
not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.
When the chief Shepherd is revealed, you will receive the crown of glory that doesn’t fade away.
Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
To him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, our faithful brother, as I consider him, I have written to you briefly, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which you stand.
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you. So does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

chapters.title: Living hope requires changed conduct and sincere love during present trials
chapters.summary: Peter writes to chosen exiles in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. He blesses God for a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. An inheritance is kept in heaven for them. For a little while trials grieve them and test their faith like gold. The prophets searched for this salvation. The readers are to be holy, for they were redeemed with Christ’s precious blood. They are to love one another from the heart. They were born again through God’s word, which remains forever.
chapters.meaning: Verses 18–19 say the readers were redeemed with the blood of Christ. Verse 22 says they have purified their souls by obeying the truth. That purifying has an aim stated in the verse: sincere brotherly affection. Then the command follows: love one another from the heart, fervently. Verse 23 gives the ground for it. They were born again of seed that does not perish. Verses 24–25 contrast that with grass, which withers.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects trials with living hope and belonging to God. Why does a secure inheritance lead into sincere love rather than private confidence alone?

chapters.historicalNote: The greeting addresses scattered hearers as chosen people whose inheritance remains secure beyond present loss. Resurrection supplies living hope while the gold comparison gives trials a place within tested faith. The prophets' earlier search connects the received message with service directed toward these hearers. Hope therefore leads into prepared minds and conduct that differs from former desires. Redemption through precious blood contrasts with silver and gold that cannot preserve lasting life. The ending makes sincere love the result of received truth rather than private security.

chapters.title: A shared spiritual house stands beside unequal power and the refusal of revenge
chapters.summary: Peter tells them to put away malice and to long for pure milk. They come to Christ, a living stone, and are built into a spiritual house. They are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, and a holy nation. They once were not a people and now are God’s people. As foreigners they should live well among the Gentiles. They should be subject to kings and governors for the Lord’s sake. Servants should be subject even to harsh masters. Christ suffered for them and left an example.
chapters.meaning: Verse 18 tells servants to submit even to harsh masters. Verse 20 says there is no credit in bearing a deserved beating. Bearing unjust suffering is what God commends. Verse 21 gives Christ as the example for that case. Verse 23 says what he did not do: he did not curse back or threaten. He entrusted himself to the one who judges justly. Verse 24 adds that he bore our sins in his body on the tree.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects Christ's example with faithful conduct during trials. How does the refusal of revenge place judgment beyond the present power of harsh masters?

chapters.historicalNote: Milk and living stones connect personal growth with being built together as God's people. The stone's rejection shows why public disapproval need not decide the value of that belonging. Instructions about rulers and masters then place good conduct within existing unequal power. Brown reads the direct address to bound workers as giving vulnerable hearers a meaningful role. Yet the commands retain subjection even to harsh masters rather than abolishing that relationship. Christ's refusal of revenge leaves judgment with God while his suffering grounds righteous life.

chapters.title: Shared inheritance and gentle witness frame the argument about suffering and rescue
chapters.summary: Wives are told to be subject to their husbands and to value a gentle spirit. Husbands are told to honor their wives as joint heirs of life. All should be compassionate and not repay evil for evil. Peter quotes a psalm about seeking peace. If they suffer for righteousness, they are blessed. They should be ready to answer anyone who asks about their hope. Christ suffered once, the righteous for the unrighteous. He spoke to the spirits in prison, and baptism now saves.
chapters.meaning: Verse 15 tells them to be ready with an answer about their hope. It adds the manner: with humility and fear. Verse 16 adds a third condition, a good conscience. The reason is practical. They are being spoken against as evildoers. A good way of life disappoints those who curse it. Verse 17 says suffering for doing good is better than for doing evil.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson reads the imprisoned spirits through Christ's visit to the spirit world. Why must an answer about hope include humility and a good conscience?

chapters.historicalNote: The household directions ask wives to influence unbelieving husbands through conduct while retaining unequal roles. Husbands must give honor because their wives share the inheritance of life. The wider assembly then receives instructions against returning harm with harm or insult with insult. An answer about hope must include humility and a good conscience rather than aggressive defense. Christ's suffering leads into the difficult account of imprisoned spirits and Noah's rescue through water. The baptism comparison emphasizes conscience before God through resurrection rather than removal of bodily dirt.

chapters.title: Changed conduct needs shared service when former companions respond with insults
chapters.summary: Peter says Christ suffered in the flesh, and the readers should have the same mind. They have spent enough time in the ways of the Gentiles. Former companions think it strange and speak evil of them. The end of all things is near, so they should be sober and pray. Above all they should love one another earnestly, for love covers many sins. They should be hospitable without grumbling and use their gifts to serve. They should not be surprised at the fiery trial. If anyone suffers as a Christian, he should not be ashamed.
chapters.meaning: Verse 4 says former companions now speak evil of the readers. The next verses turn to life inside the group. Verse 8 asks for earnest love, and verse 9 for hospitality without grumbling. Verse 10 gives the rule for every member. Each has received a gift and is to use it to serve others. The verse calls them managers of God’s grace, which takes many forms. Verse 11 names two kinds of gift: speaking and serving.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects teaching to the dead with God's just judgment. How do hospitality and received gifts make love practical during insult and pressure?

chapters.historicalNote: The account of Christ's suffering introduces a break with the hearers' former ways of living. Former companions find that refusal strange and respond with evil speech. The statement about the dead places judgment beside the possibility of life in the spirit. Expectation of the end then calls for sober prayer rather than disorder or neglect. Hospitality and received gifts make mutual service the practical shape of continued love. The distinction separates suffering for Christian faith from suffering caused by murder, theft, or interference.

chapters.title: Leadership by example and shared humility answer danger without ruling through fear
chapters.summary: Peter writes to the elders as a fellow elder who saw Christ’s sufferings. They are to shepherd God’s flock willingly, not for gain. They are not to lord it over the flock but to be examples. When the chief Shepherd appears, they will receive a crown of glory. The younger should be subject to the elder, and all should be humble. They should cast their worries on God, who cares for them. The devil prowls like a roaring lion, and they should resist him. Peter writes through Silvanus and sends greetings from Babylon and from Mark.
chapters.meaning: Verse 2 gives three contrasts for elders, and verse 3 is the third. They serve willingly, not under pressure. They serve eagerly, not for dishonest gain. They lead by example, not by lording it over the flock. The flock is called “those entrusted to you,” so it is not theirs. Verse 4 names the chief Shepherd, who will appear. Verse 5 then asks humility of everyone, elders included.

lds.text: How does the chief Shepherd's promised appearance limit the authority of present leaders?

chapters.historicalNote: The speaker addresses elders as a fellow elder rather than placing care beyond shared responsibility. The flock comparison requires willing service instead of greed, force, or domination. The promised chief Shepherd makes present leaders answerable within a task they do not own. Humility includes younger hearers and the whole assembly, while God's care supports handing over worries. The lion comparison calls for alert resistance alongside knowledge that other believers also face suffering. The closing greetings place this appeal within shared workers rather than an isolated instruction.

people.name: Peter
people.role: Apostle of Jesus Christ and fellow elder
people.relations: He writes to believers in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. He sends the letter through Silvanus.
people.meaning: Peter greets believers living as foreigners in the Dispersion. He tells the elders to shepherd the flock willingly. They must not lord it over those in their care. He calls himself a witness of the sufferings of Christ. He sends greetings from Babylon and from Mark, his son.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jesus Christ
people.role: Christ who suffered, rose, and is at God’s right hand
people.relations: Peter calls him the chief cornerstone and the chief Shepherd. He is also the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
people.meaning: Peter says God raised Jesus Christ from the dead. Christ suffered for us and left an example. When he was cursed, he did not curse back. He trusted the one who judges righteously. Peter says believers will receive a crown when the chief Shepherd is revealed.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sarah
people.role: Holy woman who called Abraham lord
people.relations: Peter names her obeying her husband Abraham. He calls his readers her children if they do well.
people.meaning: Peter tells wives to be gentle and quiet. He says holy women of the past did so. He says Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. Wives are her children if they do well. They must not be put in fear by any terror.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abraham
people.relations: Peter says Sarah obeyed him and called him lord.
people.meaning: Peter names Abraham only as the one Sarah obeyed. He tells no story about him. The next verse tells husbands to honor their wives as joint heirs.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Noah
people.role: Man in whose days the ship was built
people.relations: Peter names his days, when God waited patiently. Eight souls were saved through water.
people.meaning: Peter says some spirits in prison were disobedient in the days of Noah. God waited patiently while the ship was built. Eight souls were saved through water. Peter calls this a symbol of baptism.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Silvanus
people.role: Faithful brother who helped write the letter
people.relations: Peter calls him our faithful brother, as he considers him.
people.meaning: Peter says he wrote this brief letter through Silvanus. The letter says nothing more about what Silvanus did. Peter says the letter shows the true grace of God.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
